title: The canonical Cech comparison map is an isomorphism for affine-intersection covers
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal U:X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ be an open covering such that $U_{i_0\dots i_p}$ is affine for all $p\geq0$ and all $i_0,\dots,i_p\in I$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Then for every $p\geq0$ the canonical comparison map $c_{\mathcal F}:\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ of [lem-sc-cech-comparison-map-naturality] is an isomorphism; it is the identification $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ of [lem-pc-cech-computes].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma Tag 01XD (coherent-lemma-cech-cohomology-quasi-coherent), proved via Cohomology of Sheaves, Lemma Tag 01ET (cohomology-lemma-cech-spectral-sequence-application, degeneration of the Cech-to-cohomology spectral sequence, whose edge map is the canonical map of Tag 01EQ) and Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma Tag 01XB (cohomology of quasi-coherent modules on affines vanishes)

proof.text: Let $p\geq0$. By [lem-sc-cech-comparison-map-naturality] the canonical comparison map $c_{\mathcal F}:\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ is defined for every $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ and every open covering $\mathcal U$ of $X$. Under the present hypotheses (all finite intersections $U_{i_0\dots i_p}$ affine, $\mathcal F$ quasi-coherent), which are exactly those of [lem-pc-cech-computes], that node gives the identification $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ for all $p\geq0$, the identification being the canonical comparison map $c_{\mathcal F}$ (Stacks 01XD states that the map of 01EQ, which [lem-sc-cech-comparison-map-naturality] defines, is an isomorphism). Hence $c_{\mathcal F}$ is an isomorphism for every $p$, and it is the identification of [lem-pc-cech-computes].
